question.text: Resistance of a conductivity cell (cell constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>129</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>) filled with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>74</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>ppm</mi></math> solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KCl</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> (labelled as solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math>). When the same cell is filled with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KCl</mi></math> solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>149</mn><mi>ppm</mi></math>, the resistance is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> (labelled as solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>). The ratio of molar conductivity of solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> and solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> is i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mo>∧</mo><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mo>∧</mo><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is____Given, molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KCl</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>74</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Given lA=129 m-1

KCl solution 1:

74.5ppm,   R1=100 Ω

KCl solution 2:

149ppm,    R2=50 Ω

Here, ppm1ppm2=M1M2

and κ = 1RG*   where G* = cell constant

Since value of cell constant is same in both the cases.

k1k2 = R2R1

∧1∧2=k1×1000M1k2×1000M2

=K1 K2×M2M1 = R2 R1×M2M1

=50100×14974.5 = 1

=∧1∧2=1,000×10-3
